acquisition: Prior, parameter geometry, covariance/radii, and loss are supplied. For N46 use, acquire an accuracy net and a quantitative mixture/channel modulus; neither follows from the Gaussian lemma.
alignment: N07 and N30 share a one-observation blind encoder, fresh-output decoder, total input-dependent memory dimension D, and posterior small-ball/POVM trace-mass converse. N46/N61 are prospective destinations or stress controls, not already aligned instances.
assumptions: Finite-spanning prior and a posterior statistic m(x) with nondegenerate covariance on an event of positive probability.
Uniform target loss controls squared posterior-statistic distortion over every decoder output.
All retained input-dependent registers count toward D; no free entangled reference or retained real side record.
cost: D=sum_j d_j; include net size and any channel acquisition cost in an N46 application. N30 finite-bit compilation, physical model comparison, and growing-dimension constants remain additional costs.
falsifier: A destination experiment with vanishing target loss but nonvanishing posterior-score distortion, or with useful score small-ball geometry only on a vanishing-probability set. N61 is a stress test against inferring EB reconstruction from marginal broadcasting alone.
missing_lemma: Prove uniform loss-to-posterior-score control and positive-probability posterior small-ball geometry for the destination experiment; for N46 also connect fidelity/broadcast loss to that score and quantify the net/mixture modulus.

reciprocity.forward: Gaussian posterior-volume mechanism may transfer only when destination supplies matching score, loss, and small-ball geometry.
reciprocity.reverse: An N46/N61 converse transfers back to Gaussian memory only if its full-algebra/fidelity or broadcast hypotheses imply N07/N30's one-sample TV risk and posterior-score distortion bounds; no such reverse implication is supplied.

scope: Reusable proof pattern hypothesis, not a new lower bound, full N46 application, or claim that N61 refutes geometry-conditioned converses.
